show_title: Capital Allocators – Inside the Institutional Investment Industry
title: WTT: The Real Yale Model

reader_summary.headline: A few weeks ago, somewhere on a sunny beach.
reader_summary.overview: A few weeks ago, somewhere on a sunny beach. I found a few gems in his words that struck me as quite different from how his teachings were interpreted by the industry. This blog highlights those differences. The Real Yale Model investors following David Swenson too often missed the mark in their interpretation of his theory.

key_points.text: A few weeks ago, somewhere on a sunny beach.
key_points.evidence_quote: A few weeks ago, somewhere on a sunny beach, I sat down with David Swenson's revised edition of Pioneering Portfolio Management that he wrote just before the financial crisis and published in 2009, nine years after his original work.

key_points.text: Like children playing the game telephone, they listen to other voices and echo beliefs with shakier foundations than Yale's.
key_points.evidence_quote: Like children playing the game telephone, they listen to other voices and echo beliefs with shakier foundations than Yale's.

key_points.text: Anyone adopting the Yale model is well served to revisit David's writing from time to time.
key_points.evidence_quote: Anyone adopting the Yale model is well served to revisit David's writing from time to time.

key_points.text: I had a chance to do that and found perspectives on illiquid investments, asset allocation, active management, private equity, and rebalancing.
key_points.evidence_quote: I had a chance to do that and found perspectives on illiquid investments, asset allocation, active management, private equity, and rebalancing, that differ from the conventional wisdom that defines the Yale model.
